### Speaker notes

> Riding the waves – where we are today
> Four years ago, GenAI began to fundamentally change software development. That shift has come in three waves – and today we're living in the transition where agents eventually become full-fledged team-members.
> Wave 1 – it rode along and helped you write code faster, but the developer did all the driving.
> Wave 2 – Agents moved from assisting to participating as peers – planning, building, and reviewing across the lifecycle. Some teams are still dipping their toes in; many businesses are already rolling out at scale.
> Wave 3 – Teams and agents work in tandem, with the developer at the center directing the work. That's where the world is rapidly heading.
> So today we're squarely in the shift from Wave 2 to Wave 3 – the pair programmer becoming a true peer and teammate, with developers at the center.

### On-slide text

- Plan
- Build

### Speaker notes

> We’re in a new era of software development. Agents aren’t just helping developers write code...
> They’re now participating in the lifecycle. They plan, they build, they review.
> They’re becoming collaborators in how you build and ship software.
> But the agentic shift also led to disjointed workflows, more context switching, and too much time spent reviewing agent-generated code. Most developer tools were not designed for directing multiple agents in parallel. You lose track of what's running.

## Slide 4

### On-slide text

- _No extractable text; the slide is primarily visual._

### Speaker notes

> This is where GitHub Copilot has been expanding: not just one tool in one place, but AI that works where developers already are. The core idea is: code, command, and collaborate.
> Copilot is designed to support different needs — whether you care most about speed, accuracy, cost, or flexibility.
> It also supports different ways of working: GitHub Copilot agents, custom agents, third-party agents, and integrations across the tools developers already use.
> So instead of thinking about Copilot as “just autocomplete,” we should think about it as a broader AI platform across the developer workflow.

## Slide 7

### On-slide text

- So how do we bring it
- all together?
- Plan
- Build
- Review
- Ship
- USER
- AI

### Speaker notes

> Most developer tools were not designed for directing multiple agents in parallel. Context scatters across windows. You lose track of what’s running. Code lands in pull requests without a clear trail of what the agent tried, what it validated, or where human judgment is needed.
> You generate something… it looks right… and then:
> the context is lost as you switch tools
> the work can’t be safely executed or validated
> the team doesn’t trust it enough to ship
> The issue isn’t capability. It’s everything that happens around the code.
> None of that gets solved with a better prompt. Because what’s missing isn’t a feature...
